ideas_declared.rationale: Decomposition component 1/3 of the note's p.2 headline rule: the band-touch condition alone, with the 200MA regime gate removed. Exit is the mid-band (SMA20) touch, i.e. 'reversion to the mean achieved' -- this doubles as the band-touch-as-exit test from note p.9, using the middle band as the (partial) reversion target.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
ideas_declared.source: note p.2 headline rule, decomposed: band-touch component alone

ideas_declared.rationale: Decomposition component 2/3 of the note's p.2 headline rule: the 200MA regime gate alone, with the band-touch condition removed. Same expression as the trend-ma stream's regime_filter_standalone and the prior study's momentum_persistence, run here as this stream's own decomposition baseline, not claimed as a fresh replication.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
ideas_declared.source: note p.2 headline rule, decomposed: 200MA gate alone

ideas_declared.rationale: Decomposition component 3/3, and the note's headline rule verbatim (p.2): 'IF price > 200 MA AND price < lower BB THEN Buy'. This is the exact expression behind the smoke-test numbers this stream exists to reproduce and extend (SPY edge +0.134, n_indep=87, p=0.0075; QQQ edge +0.099, n_indep=63, p=0.153 -- both from a 2-test family, re-corrected here across the full 8x5 family). Exit uses the opposite (upper) band as the full mean-reversion target, the note p.9 band-touch-exit concept applied to the headline rule itself.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
ideas_declared.source: note p.2, headline entry logic, verbatim

ideas_declared.rationale: note p.5 z-score entry band, |0.5| < z < |2|, oversold/long construction: price is moderately below its 20-day mean (more than half a band-half-width, less than a full band-half-width) -- the note's 'stretched rubber band, likely to snap back' zone. Exit at the mid-band, i.e. the z=0 line.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
ideas_declared.source: note p.5, z-score banded entry |0.5| < z < |2|

ideas_declared.rationale: note p.5's hard-stop reasoning, tested as an empirical claim rather than wired in as a position-management stop (the DSL's stop_loss_pct is a price-percentage field, not a z-score-conditioned one, so the literal 'exit the position if z exceeds 3' mechanism is not directly expressible -- see 'what this cannot express'). Same direction, exit, horizon and holding cap as zscore_oversold_band, differing only in how far below the mean the entry requires: if the note's reasoning holds (extreme deviation is trend, not a stretched rubber band), this entry's edge should be weaker than, not stronger than, the moderate band's.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: extreme-deviation (z<-3) entries do not show a weaker 20-bar edge than the moderate band (zscore_oversold_band) -- if the edges are equal or the extreme entry is stronger, the note's stop-out reasoning is not supported
ideas_declared.source: note p.5, hard stop at |z| > 3 ('large deviation means a strong trend, not a stretched rubber band')

ideas_declared.rationale: note p.5: bandwidth < 5% => compression / consolidating regime, i.e. a breakout is coming. Uses the note's own 5% threshold on (upper-lower)/mid -- NOT the prior study's volatility_contraction template, which used (upper-lower) < close*0.04, a 4% threshold on a DIFFERENT denominator (close, not the mid band). That discrepancy is reported, not silently reconciled. The note's claim is direction-agnostic (a breakout can go either way); the harness's hit-rate statistic is not, so this idea tests only the directional half of the claim and the report reads median forward return alongside hit rate to keep that limitation visible rather than overclaiming a directional finding.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline

ideas_declared.rationale: note p.5: bandwidth > 15% => high-volatility trending regime. Same directional-statistic caveat as bb_bandwidth_compression: 'trending' does not itself specify up or down, so this tests whether wide-band conditions on this long-biased universe skew up, alongside the strategy mechanics' own volatility metric.
ideas_declared.falsifies_if: 20-bar forward hit rate does not exceed the same-bars baseline
ideas_declared.source: note p.5, BB bandwidth > 15% => high-volatility trending regime
